attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post. He states them in his own voice and endorses them.

semantics.note: 'You'd be wrong' says flatly that the overactive guardrail problem was still unsolved in Feb 2024. The investment and model-size part is kept as background. This is an observation, not a forecast.

contract.note: The plain reading (major deployed assistants still sometimes refused benign requests) is fair and ordinary. It does not require every system to fail. Taking 'now' as Feb 2024 up to the post date fits the text.

evidence.note: Daily Dot reporter test dated Feb 21, 2024: Gemini refused to make a photo of a white or a Black person. A dated, independent test of a benign request inside the target period.

Google's Feb 23, 2024 post. Google admits the model became overly cautious, misread benign prompts as sensitive, and should not refuse any group. This backs the mechanism, but it is a company disclosure and dates no specific refusal.

reviews.rationale: e1 is an independent, dated test (Feb 21, 2024) in which Gemini, a major deployed assistant, refused an ordinary image request. Google's own retrospective (e2) admits it wrongly refused anodyne prompts. Nothing in the packet shows the refusals were justified or that excessive refusals had ended. The support condition is met.
